record.title: CAMR: Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay for Continual Learning in Large Language Models
record.abstract: Continual learning requires large language models to acquire new knowledge and capabilities while retaining what they have learned. Fine-tuning and replay support acquisition and retention, but deciding whether incoming examples need supervision and which historical examples to revisit remains a challenge. We propose Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay (CAMR), an adaptive framework that jointly controls current-example supervision and historical replay. CAMR combines compatibility checks with a learned memory gate to guide an online policy over three actions: learning incoming examples with general replay, jointly reinforcing compatible related examples, and skipping direct supervision of verified mastered duplicates. The policy learns from acquisition, retention, and training-cost feedback under a bounded per-arrival replay budget. We evaluate CAMR with Qwen3-8B-Base on continual factual updating and cross-task and cross-domain learning. On WikiBigEdit, CAMR consistently leads evaluated methods in Original Match from 3K to 100K facts, reaching 93.66% after just 3K facts and surpassing Full-history Replay (LoRA) after 100K facts. It also achieves the highest final scores on all four selected TRACE tasks and maintains or improves earlier-task performance relative to post-acquisition levels in a sequence spanning financial question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and summarization.

record.title: Neuronal Identity as an Organizational Basis for Analyzing Neural Population Dynamics
record.abstract: Individual neurons exhibit diverse molecular, morphological, and electrophysiological properties that shape their distinct roles in neural circuits. While these multimodal features are largely shared across individuals, they remain an underutilized source of information in analyzing neural population dynamics. We posit that these shared biological profiles provide a common reference for relating neural dynamics across subjects and recording sessions. Our framework leverages this structure by routing neurons into latent groups based on their biological profiles and analyzing population dynamics through group-level representations. Because these assignments are anchored in biological properties that are consistent across subjects, the learned organization supports transfer to unseen animals without retraining or neuron-wise correspondence. We evaluate our framework on whole-brain calcium imaging in larval zebrafish and large-scale electrophysiology in the mouse visual cortex. Across both species and recording modalities, the framework delivers state-of-the-art performance in both neural decoding and manifold analysis: it achieves superior decoding of behavior and stimulus labels while better preserving the temporal consistency and local geometric structure of latent trajectories on unseen data. Our experiments demonstrate that not only does providing biological features improve baseline performance, but our proposed framework achieves even stronger results by using these properties to explicitly structure the population rather than treating them as auxiliary inputs. Together, these results suggest that organizing neural populations by their multimodal biological features offers a promising framework for generalizing population dynamics across subjects and recording sessions.

record.title: ODAT-SE: A modular and parallel framework for simulation-based inverse problems
record.abstract: Open Data Analysis Tool for Science and Engineering (ODAT-SE) is an open-source Python framework for inverse problems that are solved by repeated forward simulations. It succeeds 2DMAT, which was developed for surface-structure analysis with quantum-beam diffraction and has since been applied to other fields. In version 3, the search algorithms were separated from the application-specific solvers, which became independent packages, and the software was renamed; this paper describes the current version 4.0. The framework connects optimization and sampling algorithms to solvers through a common interface for parameter mapping, constraints, and objective evaluation, so that an existing simulation code can be used with any of the algorithms. Relative to the previously published 2DMAT, it provides two-level MPI parallelism, which distributes candidate evaluations over processes and each evaluation over a parallel solver, checkpoint and continuation facilities, random search, global optimizers from SciPy, tensor-train optimization, and a Bayesian workflow that estimates partition-function ratios, model evidence, effective noise levels, and marginal posterior distributions. We validate the Bayesian workflow against closed-form results for a linear regression, benchmark tensor-train optimization on continuous, binary, and mixed-integer problems, and verify the two-level parallelization by the same optimum for all process decompositions. Taking up the positron-diffraction example of the 2DMAT paper, the workflow identifies the correlated structural solutions and an effective noise scale close to the imposed perturbation, while exposing incomplete convergence of symmetry-related mode weights. Solver packages, templates, and a gallery of examples support the use of the framework as a general platform for inverse-problem analysis.

record.title: Axiom: a logic programming language to express and enforce network designs
record.abstract: Human errors remain the leading cause of network outages. To prevent them researchers propose general verifiers that analyze the network behavior. Yet, their (symbolic) models struggle to accurately reflect network devices, they fail to scale to large networks, and report misbehavior, not what configuration line caused it. We attribute all three challenges to specifications that describe the intended behavior but not how operators intend to achieve it---the network's design: which protocols to run and how to combine them. We present Axiom, a language for expressing network designs, and a checker that finds every violation and the responsible commands. Operators state their design decision as rules over configuration commands. Axiom then compiles them into a single Datalog program that checks the entire network directly on its configurations, not on the state they produce. Our prototype checks a 754-router network within seconds. Ultimately, a design enforced on every keystroke could give network operators the integrated development environment that programmers have long enjoyed.

record.title: Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions
record.abstract: High-frequency control problems are often studied through time discretization, but refining the timestep $δ$ increases the discrete horizon $H=T/δ$ and can make standard finite-horizon regret guarantees deteriorate even when the physical horizon $T$ is fixed. We study episodic value-based reinforcement learning for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions. The performance is measured as the cumulative regret over $K$ episodes relative to the optimal policy of the corresponding Euler model. Under stability and regularity conditions on value function gradients, Bellman residual derivatives, and fitted critics, we prove an $\mathcal{O}(\log K)$ regret bound with constants uniform in $δ$. For dynamics with drift linear in unknown parameters and unknown constant diffusion covariance, we verify localized versions of these conditions for a constrained, model-based controlled-diffusion fitted-$Q$ algorithm (CD-FQ) and obtain high-probability $\mathcal{O}(\log K\log\log K)$ regret for fixed and finite $T$, again with constants uniform in $δ$.

record.title: DocSkill: Skill-Integrated Agentic Reasoning for Multilingual Multi-Hop Document Question Answering
record.abstract: Multilingual multi-hop document question answering (MMHop-DocQA) requires locating and integrating evidence across complex layouts, document pages, and diverse languages. Existing approaches include single-pass processing and adaptive tool use, but learning to coordinate evidence acquisition, cross-page integration, and answer verification remains challenging. To address this challenge, we present DocSkill, an agentic framework with a learned skill-orchestration policy for adaptive evidence acquisition and reasoning. The policy selects, revisits, or skips skills according to the evolving evidence state. To construct supervision for skill orchestration, bounded Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) explores alternative skill trajectories offline. These trajectories provide demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and preference pairs for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). We further introduce MMHop-DocBench, a multilingual multi-hop document QA dataset with training and test splits, containing 60K QA pairs across 10 languages and eight document domains. Its HopGen pipeline builds hierarchical page-element graphs to derive traceable cross-page evidence paths and generate grounded QA pairs with page- and element-level evidence annotations. Experiments show that DocSkill with Qwen3-VL-8B achieves 41.0 accuracy and 49.2 F1 on MMHop-DocBench, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 5.5 and 6.3 points, respectively, and achieving competitive performance on MMLongBench-Doc and DocBench.

record.title: GeoGSplat: Geometry-Grounded Non-Pixel-Aligned Gaussian Splatting
record.abstract: Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting enables efficient novel view synthesis, but pixel-aligned prediction makes the primitive count grow with image resolution and view count, leading to substantial redundancy and increased computational cost. Non-pixel-aligned methods address this limitation by predicting a fixed number of Gaussians. Without explicit ray and depth constraints, these methods yield misplaced Gaussian centers, causing rendering artifacts under large viewpoint changes. To address this issue, we introduce GeoGSplat, a geometry-grounded feed-forward model that explicitly incorporates geometric priors into the non-pixel-aligned framework. A dual-branch encoder constructs Anchors and Triplane to capture coarse 3D structure and fine-grained scene features, respectively. Subsequently, a hierarchical decoder progressively decodes dense 3D points and Gaussian primitives, enabling 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis. GeoGSplat surpasses both state-of-the-art pixel-aligned and non-pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting methods on DTU and NRGBD in terms of novel view synthesis and reconstruction. The advantage of our geometry-grounded paradigm further increases as target viewpoints move farther from the input cameras, demonstrating stronger generalization to large viewpoint changes. Project Page: https://comedy0913.github.io/projects/geogsplat

record.title: Making Self-Driving Laboratories Auditable:A Unified Framework for Hybrid Actions,Measurements, and Safe Execution
record.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are laboratory systems that couple experimental planning, automated execution, and measurement feedback in a closed loop. Integrating flexible robot control with the typed application programming interfaces (APIs) and continuous measurements exposed by laboratory instruments remains an execution-interface challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a traceable framework comprising four components: LAM (Lab Action Model), OpenSDL, Safe-SDL, and L3-Bench. LAM is a proposed measurement-conditioned policy architecture that extends vision-language-action paradigms to generate both continuous robot trajectories and typed instrument API calls. OpenSDL is an execution substrate with an initial control implementation, designed to map role-level operations to heterogeneous devices, coordinate execution, and record timestamped causal events. The proposed Safe-SDL runtime gate combines pre-dispatch schema and resource checks with signal temporal logic monitoring during execution, including extended waiting periods. L3-Bench (Level-3 Laboratory Benchmark) specifies an episode-level evaluation protocol covering physical outcomes, timing, reproducibility, safety violations, and fault recovery. Together, these components provide an end-to-end design for linking hybrid action generation, monitored device execution, measurement feedback, and experimental evaluation, addressing coordination and traceability challenges in SDL workflows.

record.title: Bayesian Treed Vecchia Gaussian Process Emulation via Sequential Monte Carlo
record.abstract: Computer models (or simulators) are used in many scientific domains to understand and predict real-world processes, but they are expensive to run. One way to address this hurdle is to use Gaussian processes (GPs). For complex physical systems such as storm surge, simulator outputs often exhibit heterogeneous structures, and many nonstationary GP methods become impractical with several inputs and tens of thousands of runs. To address these issues, we combine the divide-and-conquer idea of treed GP models with Vecchia approximations in a Bayesian treed Vecchia GP (TVGP) model. The model uses the Bayesian classification and regression tree prior for random recursive partitioning of the input domain. Within each leaf, a Vecchia approximation allows efficient likelihood evaluation. For Bayesian inference, we develop a sequential Monte Carlo algorithm that explores tree space as an alternative to reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo. The method is demonstrated on synthetic examples with two and ten inputs and on a storm-surge simulator with seven inputs and up to 50,649 training runs. TVGP has the smallest prediction error in both synthetic examples and with the larger storm-surge training set, although its predictive intervals undercover in the example with ten inputs and the storm-surge application.

record.title: Expressive Guitar Synthesis via Controllable Latent Flow Matching
record.abstract: Realistic guitar synthesis requires both audio fidelity and interpretable control over how notes are performed. The input timed MIDI events decide what is played but not how, leaving the continuous within-note decisions of guitar performance--such as pitch inflection and per-string articulation--unspecified. A model that directly maps MIDI to audio must therefore realize the performance implicitly, and users are left with limited control over the synthesized performance. We therefore propose a two-stage guitar synthesis pipeline that predicts editable, per-string $f_0$ and amplitude trajectories from timed note events and note-level dynamics, and renders them into audio using latent flow matching. Experimental results show that the proposed system outperforms a matched single-stage counterpart and DDSP-Guitar in control fidelity and perceived quality, while keeping the controls editable. Sound examples can be found online.

record.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
record.abstract: Learning controllable world dynamics from heterogeneous interaction videos is challenging because robot embodiments use incompatible action spaces, while human videos lack native control labels. We present RynnWorld-Latent, a cross-embodiment video world model that uses the 3D-grounded latent actions introduced by RynnLAM as a shared conditioning interface. This representation enables joint pretraining on human interaction videos, robot demonstrations, and simulation rollouts without requiring a common native action space. Built on a pretrained video transformer, RynnWorld-Latent combines global action tokens with an identity-initialized local pathway that aligns actions with future video latents. We pretrain on 23 datasets comprising approximately 553.5M frames and adapt the model to target robots through post-training. The framework supports two data-generation routes: digital teleoperation uses target robot commands to generate action-video demonstrations, while latent-action synthesis transfers source motion to an edited initial frame and pairs the resulting rollout with retargeted pseudo robot actions. Experiments show improved video prediction metrics on public benchmarks and two real-robot platforms, alongside qualitative action following when different action sequences share the same initial observation. Synthetic mid-training improves policy success rates on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and both generation routes improve real-world policy success rates over real-demonstration-only training in the evaluated settings. These results support universal latent actions as a scalable interface for learning controllable visual dynamics across heterogeneous embodiments.

record.title: Weakness Localization Is Not Enough: State-Aware Recursive Knowledge Improvement for Large Language Models
record.abstract: Knowledge improvement in large language models is shifting from predefined knowledge incorporation pipelines toward evaluation-guided updating. Existing methods use evaluation to localize model-specific knowledge weaknesses and guide targeted post-training. However, identifying what to improve does not necessarily provide sufficient information for deciding how to improve it. The same localized weakness can be compatible with distinct operational knowledge states: the relevant knowledge may be unavailable, available but difficult to access reliably, or accessible but ineffective for downstream use. We call this ambiguity knowledge-state aliasing. When compatible states favor different interventions, greater diagnostic resolution alone is insufficient for intervention selection. Moreover, model updates can change the underlying knowledge state before the observed weakness disappears, such that an intervention appropriate in one round may no longer address the bottleneck in the next. To address these challenges, we propose Recursive Knowledge Improvement (RKI), which formulates knowledge improvement as a sequential, state-aware intervention process. RKI organizes knowledge into graph-structured units that provide a shared basis for diagnostic evaluation and targeted intervention across rounds. At each round, RKI localizes knowledge weaknesses, estimates the model's operational knowledge state from diagnostic evidence and intervention history, selects a corresponding intervention, and re-evaluates the updated model before determining the next intervention. On HotpotEval and SafeInternalEval, RKI outperforms existing knowledge incorporation methods by 18.41 points on average. Further analyses show that knowledge states provide additional guidance for intervention selection beyond weakness localization and can change across model updates even when the observed weakness persists.

record.title: An Incremental Knowledge-Graph Learner Digital Twin for Evidence-Grounded Early Warning
record.abstract: Early-warning models in learning analytics can identify learners at risk of failure or withdrawal, but the resulting alerts are often only weakly connected to inspectable learning evidence. A risk score may indicate that intervention is needed without showing which traces, assessment events, or temporal patterns justify the alert. This paper introduces an incremental Learner Digital Twin for evidence-grounded early warning, implemented as a lightweight knowledge graph. The twin is updated at temporal checkpoints by replaying learning traces and assessment records, and it serves both as a feature-extraction substrate and as an explanation-grounding substrate. Predictive features are derived through graph-mediated queries, while features, attributions, alerts, evidence items, and raw records are represented as queryable graph entities. The framework is instantiated and evaluated on a public learning-analytics benchmark under a temporal protocol. The results show that graph-mediated feature extraction preserves the predictive behavior of equivalent raw-table features across model families and checkpoints. Generated alerts are materialized as evidence chains linking risk decisions to feature attributions, evidence items, and raw platform records. The study shows that early-warning prediction can be routed through a semantic and provenance-aware representation while preserving predictive performance and adding traceability, verifiability, and evidence-grounded explanation.

record.title: TAPESTRY: A Single Backbone for Video Generation and Robot Control
record.abstract: Pretrained video generation models encode rich priors about physical interactions, but leveraging them for robot control typically requires either resource-intensive video generation at test time or action heads trained from scratch that do not fully utilize the pretrained backbone. We introduce Tokenizing Actions as Video Patches in a Shared Transformer Policy (TAPESTRY), a world action model that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion transformer into a robotic policy without requiring video generation at inference. Our key idea is to treat robot actions as single-patch tokens in the video model's latent space. A lightweight linear projection maps each action timestep to the patch dimensions of the pretrained VAE, and the resulting tokens are processed by the same patchifying layers and transformer backbone used for video. The shared backbone is optimized through three diffusion objectives sampled per minibatch element: Video diffusion uses VAE latents from robot and human videos to establish dynamics priors. Joint video+action diffusion trains on robot demonstrations using a coupled diffusion timestep and an asymmetric attention mask. Action-only diffusion denoises actions conditioned on clean image latents. At test time, the model generates a compact action token sequence in a single DDIM step from pure noise, producing smooth action chunks at 84 ms per action chunk on consumer hardware and avoiding the cost of full video generation. Across simulation benchmarks and real-robot experiments, TAPESTRY achieves strong performance with substantially lower inference cost than comparable joint video--action policies. More information can be found at https://tapestry-wam.github.io.

record.title: Dynamic Merging Mutually-Distilled Multi-View Networks for RGB-Event-based Representation Learning
record.abstract: Multi-modal fusion algorithms combining conventional frame-based cameras and event cameras have recently attracted substantial research attention. Typically, existing approaches convert event streams into frames, voxels, or tensors, and then learn the required spatiotemporal information from these transformed event representations for fusion with conventional frame-camera data. Obviously, such paradigms only exploit the limited representational capacity of event data. Moreover, standard training pipelines fail to fully leverage diverse model parameters obtained throughout the learning process. In this paper, we propose a novel mutual distillation method leveraging multi-view teacher network weights to better integrate multiple event representations and achieve model-parameter level fusion. Specifically, we employ multiple encoders to extract different types of event representations and perform mutual knowledge distillation at both the feature-level and logit-level in this process. Afterwards, we perform a dynamic hierarchical model merge strategy on the model parameters from the first stage to yield a unified multi-modal RGB-Event representation model. Experimental results across multiple event-based datasets demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves significant performance improvements.

record.title: AxisQ: Depth-Adaptive Channel--Frequency Quantization for Camouflaged Object Detection
record.abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) depends on weak texture and boundary cues that can be destroyed by aggressive post-training quantization (PTQ). Existing PTQ methods mainly optimize quantizers or reconstruct network blocks, while using a single precision-allocation domain throughout hierarchical backbones. Instead, we introduce AxisQ, a depth-adaptive bit-allocation framework motivated by the observation that the useful allocation axis changes with feature depth. Under a fixed per-layer average activation-bit budget, AxisQ allocates precision in the channel domain for shallow features and in the local-frequency domain for deep features, using COD-aware sensitivity to better preserve subtle foreground regions and ambiguous boundaries. We also formulate a boundary-aware Hessian approximation for reconstruction by incorporating boundary-weighted gradient and error statistics. Experiments across multiple COD models and diverse benchmarks demonstrate improved accuracy over the strongest baselines at low bit widths, with relative weighted F-measure gains of 12.7% for CFRN and 33.3% for CamoFormer-P on CAMO under W2A2 quantization. These results support adapting the allocation domain to feature depth as a transferable quantization strategy for hierarchical COD models.

record.title: Neural Simulation-Based Inference for space-time Gaussian processes
record.abstract: In spatio-temporal data analysis, estimating covariance parameters for Gaussian random fields via maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is computationally prohibitive for large datasets. Following recent advances in simulation-based inference techniques, we propose two neural network architectures - Neural Bayes Estimation (NBE) and Neural Ratio Estimation (NRE) - to learn the parameters of Gaussian spatio-temporal Gneiting-Mat{é}rn models with advection. The networks are trained on simulations generated directly from the underlying Gaussian random field model. A thorough simulation study demonstrates strong performance across one-dimensional time and both one-dimensional space and two-dimensional space, yielding high accuracy and reliable uncertainty quantification for both NBE and NRE. Through extensive offline training, the framework achieves fully amortized inference, replacing costly optimization with a single forward pass. Finally, we apply our framework to solar radiation prediction and short-term forecasting. By adopting a sliding-window approach, the model accounts for temporal non-stationarity while retaining this key advantage: achieving near-instantaneous parameter inference and forecasting.

record.title: Hyperparameter and Neural Architecture Search via Evolutionary Optimization for Reinforcement Learning: HPNAS-RL
record.abstract: In this study, we propose a dual-branch evolutionary framework that simultaneously performs Neural Architecture Search (NAS) and Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) for Reinforcement Learning (RL) in Autonomous Driving (AD) tasks. While NAS has shown strong potential in automating architecture design for Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), its application to RL remains limited, especially in scenarios that require joint optimization of architectural and training dynamics. Building on our prior work on Evolutionary Multi-Objective NAS (EMNAS), the proposed framework evolves discrete network architectures and continuous hyperparameters in parallel under a unified multi-objective search strategy. In this setup, NAS targets the convolutional layers of the RL policy network - responsible for visual feature extraction, while HPO focuses on optimizing critical RL hyperparameters. To accelerate convergence and improve generalization, we incorporate parallel evaluation and a teacher-student policy transfer mechanism. Experiments in a high-fidelity driving simulator show that the joint NAS-HPO framework consistently outperforms standalone NAS, yielding policies with higher rewards, fewer parameters, and improved stability. These results highlight the benefits of jointly optimizing model structure and training dynamics for scalable and effective RL agent design.

record.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning
record.abstract: Existing noise mitigation strategies for wind farms usually consist in reducing turbines power output, without accounting for the wake interactions between them and the noise emission directivity. This leads to over-conservative policies and unexploited wind power. Yet, turbine yaw can simultaneously affect wake interactions and the direction of noise emission, offering an additional degree of freedom for farm-level noise control. We therefore propose Noise Steering, a model-free reinforcement learning (RL) strategy that jointly controls turbine yaw angles and power setpoints to maximise farm power while satisfying a local noise constraint in a defined region. To enable training at a reduced computational cost, a low-fidelity acoustic model is coupled with the steady-state FLORIS simulator. The RL agent effectively learns how to redirect wakes and noise directivity away from the protected region while redistributing power across the farm. On a six-turbine test farm, the policy satisfies the 40 dB noise constraint throughout the full range of turbulent winds, with an average power deficit of only 2% relative to greedy unimpeded control, and up to 7.7% at high wind speeds. In comparison, the industry-standard noise-reduced operation (NRO) baseline here generates an average power loss of 17%. When deployed in the higher-fidelity FASTFarm simulator, the policy largely retains its performance under steady and turbulent inflow, despite differences in simulation fidelity. These results demonstrate the potential of combining yaw control and power derating through RL to improve the power-noise trade-off in wind farm operation.

record.title: Perceptual Differences and Preferences in Speech Enhancement
record.abstract: Speech enhancement (SE) systems are commonly evaluated with objective metrics, with and without references, and with categorical subjective listening tests, all measuring speech quality and intelligibility. So far, it is unclear from such evaluations whether the processed speech is perceptually different or is preferred by everyday listeners. We investigate discrimination and preference as complementary dimensions of SE evaluation through crowdsourced triangle and pairwise preference tests across four SE systems, with comparisons to clean references. Results show that both listeners' ability to distinguish and whether they exhibit systematic preference vary across systems and substantially across acoustic conditions. Pairwise evaluations of objective metrics showed variable correlation with both discriminability and preference, motivating further studies into these novel aspects in speech enhancement evaluation.

record.title: ASNER: Software Architecture Recovery with Adaptive Semantic Neighborhoods and Evidence-Grounded Refinement
record.abstract: Automated software architecture recovery provides architectural context for software engineering and repository-level LLM agents. Existing methods combine structural and semantic signals, but functional relatedness does not necessarily imply shared architectural responsibility. Fixed thresholds or Top-K neighborhoods also ignore repository scale and local similarity distributions, introducing errors that propagate through clustering. Unconstrained LLM refinement may further alter correct assignments without sufficient evidence. We propose ASNER (Adaptive Semantic Neighborhoods and Evidence-Grounded Refinement for Software Architecture Recovery), based on responsibility-aware, project-adaptive relation modeling and evidence-grounded boundary verification. ASNER derives structured file responsibilities with an LLM, constructs semantic neighborhoods that adapt to repository scale and local similarity distributions, and augments a static dependency graph with selected semantic relations and weak directory cues. Community detection recovers the component backbone. A Responsibility-Ownership-Aware (ROA) Agent then examines uncertain boundary files using project-level responsibilities and traceable code evidence, changing assignments only when supported. Experiments on 12 open-source projects spanning C, C++, Java, and Python show that ASNER achieves the best macro-average on all five metrics on the common benchmark, improving ARI and c2c@66 over GAER-GAT by 19.5% and 32.9%, respectively. A downstream evaluation shows that ASNER-guided LocAgent improves file-, module-, and function-level code localization, demonstrating the value of its architectural context for repository-level software engineering tasks.

record.title: Replica Analysis of Overfitting in Vector Generalized Linear Models
record.abstract: We show how the successful recent statistical physics based theory of overfitting in Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) can be generalized to a much larger family of regression models: the so-called Vector Generalized Linear Models (VGLMs), in which not a single linear combination of covariates drives the outcome, but where one has an arbitrary finite number of such linear combinations. The latter more general and complex models can describe more sophisticated statistical patterns in data, but are even more prone to overfitting than GLMs due to their significantly larger number of parameters; this often limits their use. We show that the generalization of the overfitting theory from GLMs to VGLMs causes many mathematical challenges that were absent from the earlier work, mostly related to the increased dimensional complexity of all order parameters in the theory, but that the new problem is once more solvable using the replica method. This opens up the field to many novel and welcome applications, especially in post-genome medical inference and data analysis, where overfitting is and remains a major barrier to progress. After developing the general VGLM overfitting theory, within the replica symmetric (RS) ansatz, we illustrate its merits and its correctness via application to several relevant VGLM regression models.

record.title: Charge Loss of Proteins in vacuo: Implications for Native Mass Spectrometry and Ion Mobility
record.abstract: Abstract Native ion mobility−mass spectrometry (IM−MS) is a powerful biophysical technique for characterizing protein structure. Because individual charge states often exhibit distinct structural dynamics, accurate IM-MS measurements require charge states to be examined independently. Although anecdotal reports among mass spectrometrists suggest that protein ions can lose charges during native IM-MS experiments, a thorough investigation of this phenomenon has been lacking. Here, we demonstrate that protein ions undergo charge loss inside the mass spectrometer as a direct consequence of gas-phase collisions, potentially leading to altered charge state distributions and ion mobility data. This effect was consistently observed across two instrument platforms (Synapt G2-S and Q Exactive UHMR), both ion polarities (positive and negative mode) and for three proteins (bovine serum albumin, myoglobin, and immunoglobulin G). Systematic investigations of instrumental parameters revealed that collision gas pressure has the strongest impact on the magnitude of charge loss, and that higher charge states are more affected than lower charge states. We further show that this process is largely driven by the dissociation of salt adducts and can hence be minimized through desalting in solution or inside the mass spectrometer, prior to the first m/z-analyzer (usually a quadrupole). For collision-induced unfolding experiments, significant differences were found between fingerprints acquired with and without quadrupole selection, although it remains unclear whether this phenomenon is directly related to charge loss. Overall, our study provides fundamental insights into collision-induced charge loss as a source of error in native IM-MS measurements and discusses the relevance of quadrupole m/z-selection for improving confidence in IM studies.

record.title: Digital twin technology in engineering education: a systematic review
record.abstract: Background Digital twin (DT) technology is widely adopted in engineering practice but remains inconsistently defined and unevenly implemented in engineering education. Prior studies frequently conflate digital models, digital shadows, and bidirectionally synchronized digital twins, limiting conceptual clarity and cross-study comparability. As DTs expand into cyber-physical learning environments, clearer educational framing and evidence of learning impact are needed. Purpose This review characterizes how DT technologies are conceptualized, implemented, and evaluated in engineering education and identifies gaps in technical fidelity, pedagogical alignment, and assessment rigor. Scope/Method: A systematic literature review was conducted following PRISMA framework. Scholarly publications published between 2017 and 2025 were identified using structured database searches and screened using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The final corpus of 101 studies was analyzed for disciplinary context, DT taxonomy level, synchronization architecture, pedagogical function, and learning assessment approach. Results DT-related publications in engineering education increased sharply after 2021, with most implementations situated in manufacturing, mechanical, and civil engineering. Most studies employed partial or unidirectional DT architectures rather than fully synchronized twins. Instructional uses focused primarily on visualization, monitoring, and system exploration. Few studies employed validated instruments to measure learning outcomes, and most designs remained case-based or exploratory. Recurrent barriers included infrastructure constraints, limited faculty expertise, interoperability challenges, and ethical and governance concerns. Conclusions Current educational DT implementations exhibit rapid growth but substantial methodological heterogeneity. A unified DT classification framework that aligns technical fidelity with instructional intent is needed to support rigorous design, evaluation, and scaling of DT-enabled learning environments in engineering education.

record.title: What an Active-Dendrite Continual Learner Actually Learns: A Dead-Neuron Artifact, a Granularity Result That Did Not Survive Its Own Controls, and a Repair That Is a Damping Factor
record.publication: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
record.abstract: This record deposits the combined manuscript of three previously separate studies of dendritic context-gated protection in continual learning. The three were written independently and published separately (Zenodo records 23685865 for S1, 23685385 for S3, and 23686689 for S4); this record supersedes them as a single, self-consistent narrative, and the earlier records are retained unchanged so that their DOIs continue to resolve to the documents they were issued for. The merge was necessary because the three sets of results could not all be true at once. S1 reported that a one-parameter own-segment bias on the dendritic input is a causal repair of the missing segment-task specialization, raising the learning term in 22/22 dose cells (significant in 20/22 at n=10 paired, with Delta-ell up to +4.6, t(9)=8.1). S3 showed that this repair does not transfer: on a convolutional active-dendrite backbone the dose-response collapses to noise and final accuracy reverses. S4 showed the mechanism: the winning segment's gate value is a constant of the training run (0.565, identical to four decimals under every alternative context) and the dendritic columns remain orthogonal at their random initialization, so the context pathway is present but unused as a modulator; the repair works by saturating that gate (sigma(10+u) ~ 1) and deleting the gate outright reproduces most of its gain on MNIST and outperforms it on Fashion-MNIST. The merged manuscript rewrites its title, abstract, and conclusion so that the third result is presented as an apparent success that the fourth and fifth results overturn, rather than as a contradiction across papers. It adds a self-interrogation section asking what follows for the paper's own second finding if 'dominant segment' is not a description of a routing decision but of an argmax over near-degenerate rows: the granularity ladder, the dead-neuron artifact, and the mechanism results survive, but the strong form of the anti-specialization claim does not, and the weaker formulation is adopted throughout. All statistics are recomputed from the raw per-seed records with Holm correction within each metric family, 95% confidence intervals, and paired standardized effect sizes; after correction the S1 dose grid remains significant in 16/22 cells for both Delta-ell and Delta-average, while the ConvADNet dose grid retains no significant cell on any metric. The package contains the LaTeX source, the compiled PDF in both the Elsevier (submission) and TMLR (double-blind, anonymized) formats, all figures, the bibliography, and a machine-readable file of the recomputed statistics with the scripts that produced them. All code, per-run records, pre-registrations and dated amendments are archived in the project repository linked in the manuscript.

record.title: The Curious Case of tBu-Cz-TPA-bis-DPPO: Lowest Structural Order Among Three Deep-Blue Hosts, Yet a Smooth Hole-Only Device Response
record.abstract: Deep-blue phosphine-oxide hosts are compared by energy levels and photophysics, almost never by microstructure—yet order and film morphology are routinely read as proxies for how well a host will carry charge. Here three related hosts are compared from primary particles to film relief with documented, protocol-tested descriptors. The tert-butyl-substituted S3 host emerges as the least ordered on every scale: the lowest X-ray ordered fraction at every baseline setting, the shortest film correlation, micrometre-scale relief and the lowest decomposition temperature, while only the S1 host shows lattice fringes. Disorder, however, does not spoil its hole transport. The S3 hole-only device shows a single, nearly ideal relaxation with a capacitance close to the geometric value and an apparent hole mobility of about 5 × 10−7 cm2 V−1 s−1, comparable to that of the far better-ordered S1 host. Long-range disorder in these hosts is therefore compatible with clean hole transport, and microstructure alone is not a reliable screen for transport.

record.title: The Hexagonality Law in Real Materials III: Alloys and Hydrogen

record.abstract: Hydrogen is the enemy of titanium implants and of the zirconium tubes that hold nuclear fuel: it gathers in the metal and turns it brittle. We show that the places hydrogen can sit follow the Hexagonality Law (#66) exactly. In a close-packed metal of any stacking, per metal atom, the pairs of tetrahedral holes that share a face, and the pairs of octahedral holes that share a face, both number h, the share of hexagonal layers. Two hydrogen atoms cannot sit in one face-sharing tetrahedral pair, so at most 2 − h tetrahedral sites per atom can be filled, and a hydride MHx with hydrogen in tetrahedral sites needs the metal locally to have h ≤ 2 − x: the brittle dihydrides need fully cubic stacking. In the standard fault model of these steels and alloys, Olson and Cohen's interface energy σ is exactly twice the second-neighbour layer coupling, so it measures the distance from the law. record.title: What an Active-Dendrite Continual Learner Actually Learns: A Dead-Neuron Artifact, a Granularity Result That Did Not Survive Its Own Controls, and a Repair That Is a Damping Factor

record.abstract: This record (version 2) deposits the combined manuscript of three previously separate studies of dendritic context-gated protection in continual learning, together with the additional controls that were run after the first review of this line of work. The three original studies were written independently and published separately (Zenodo records 23685865 for S1, 23685385 for S3, and 23686689 for S4); this record supersedes them as a single, self-consistent narrative, and the earlier records are retained unchanged so that their DOIs continue to resolve to the documents they were issued for. record.abstract: Manuscript prepared for The European Physical Journal C (Regular Article). Can the decay of a metastable late-time vacuum seed a new cosmological cycle? The paper specifies a scalar potential with an explicit metastable minimum, solves the Coleman-De Luccia bounce numerically in flat space and with Einstein gravity (shooting, an independent boundary-value solution, analytic de Sitter tails; 13 executable consistency checks), and converts the action to a nucleation rate per Hubble four-volume with the measured dark-energy density as the false-vacuum energy. With all scales set by the dark energy the gravitational parameter is about 1e-60, gravitational corrections to the action are about 1e-59 and the Hawking-Moss regime is irrelevant; the decay is a flat-space process controlled by one action B = b(eta)/lambda, and nucleation within a Hubble four-volume requires B below about 287. record.title: A Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis: The Persistent Presence of Multiplicative Identity and the Identity Repositioning of the Critical Half-Scale 1/2 in GHT (II)
record.publication: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
record.abstract: The classical pointwise statement of the Riemann Hypothesis is: for every nontrivial zero ρ of the Riemann zeta function ζ, Re ρ = 1/2. This statement usually directs attention to the coordinates of infinitely many zeros taken one by one. A more upstream object-level question is: to what object do these zeros belong; where does that object come from; what is being evaluated after analytic continuation; what bears self-duality after completion; and to which complete mathematical object does the final 1/2 belong as a mature scale expression? The preceding paper, A Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis: The Persistent Presence of Multiplicative Identity and the Identity Repositioning of the Critical Half-Scale 1/2 in GHT, denoted the complete multiplicative self-dual identity by I×sd, the standard normalized real-scale background by Bsc = Rscale_norm, and wrote I×sd ≡pres Bsc^(1/2) to express the identity repositioning of the same complete multiplicative self-dual identity as the critical half-scale in the standard mature real-scale language. The present paper restates this line in full and further verifies the object identity on which it depends, so that the paper can be read independently. For Re s > 1, the Euler product and the Dirichlet series jointly determine ζ(s); together with the Möbius reciprocal and the von Mangoldt logarithmic derivative they constitute the multiplicative identity fingerprint F×. F× is not a new identity-object: it is the direct structural manifestation, within mature analytic number theory, of the continued presence of multiplicative identity. Analytic continuation supplies the central identity–readout connection of the paper. The common germ, connected continuation, and the identity theorem guarantee that the global ζ is not a second function newly born after leaving the initial domain of convergence; ζ_global(s0) is the value of that same global object, and ζ_global(ρ) = 0 means that ρ is a zero of that global object. Analytic continuation therefore locks object identity, function readout, and zero attribution at once. The completed function ξ(s) registers the added structure explicitly and, where legitimate, permits ζ to be recovered from ξ and the completion factor. Inside the critical strip, ρ is a nontrivial zero if and only if ξ(ρ) = 0, so nontrivial zeros fall exactly into the same completed object. The central chain reads H× ⇝ F× ⇝ ζ_germ ⇝ ζ_global ⇝ ξ ⇝ Rξ[ρ]. The mature zero coordinate Re ρ = 1/2 and the critical half-scale identity repositioning fixed in the preceding paper thus belong to one and the same object history. Trivial zeros cancel against the poles of Γ(s/2) at negative even integers and do not become zeros of ξ, while nontrivial zeros are precisely the zeros of ξ; their local mechanisms differ, yet both classes belong to the same global ζ and exhibit the same proof-level organization — the global object and global structure are fixed first, and concrete zeros then acquire their readouts within that structure. SRCU — Source continuity, Recoverability, Cross-channel coherence, and Uniqueness under specification — serves as a formal audit interface in this paper. The complete SRCU formalism, program implementation, positive and negative controls, attack models, and formal verification are provided in the research-expanded manuscript (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23736067). The paper ultimately returns to a simple question: what is the Riemann function? The Euler product, analytic continuation, completion, functional equation, and zeros together form a mature mathematical history that can be recovered layer by layer, and the object identity jointly carried by these formulas thereby returns to the foreground. 稿件信息 / Manuscript information 作者 / Author: 任毅飞 (Yifei Ren), Independent Researcher, ORCID 0009-0009-1373-9609 版本 / Version: v2.0.5 | 日期 / Date: 2026-10-28 MSC 2020: 11M26 (Primary); 11M06, 03A05 (Secondary) 文件 / Files: RH_II_Formal_ZH.pdf(中文版); RH_II_Formal_EN.pdf (English version)配套软件 / Accompanying software: RH Core Identity Validation v1.0.1(DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23816137),§14 的 SRCU 形式审计即由其实现 前文 / Preceding paper: 10.5281/zenodo.23663855 | 研究扩展稿 / Research-expanded manuscript: 10.5281/zenodo.23736067 许可 / License: CC BY 4.0

record.title: Gradient flow of magnetic inclination and intensity as a GPS-free guidance mechanism
record.abstract: It is well established that some animals, such as sea turtles, sense the Earth's magnetic field and use it as a primary cue for long-distance navigation across the vast and featureless ocean. This remarkable ability has inspired the development of bio-inspired magnetic navigation (BIMN), which seeks to mimic these animals to develop robust and frugal navigation methods. BIMN exploits the Earth's magnetic field, sometimes described as ''Nature's GPS'', as a natural navigation infrastructure, providing a potential alternative to vulnerable satellite navigation systems. However, unlike geographic coordinates, magnetic coordinates extracted from the Earth's magnetic field do not provide a one-to-one mapping to geographic locations. Different locations can exhibit similar magnetic signatures, creating ambiguity and making BIMN inherently more challenging. Despite this fundamental challenge, we demonstrate that, within predefined regions of the Earth, magnetic inclination and intensity provide sufficient information to navigate to any destination. By formulating BIMN as a gradient flow control and guidance problem, we show that the resulting gradient flow act as current that carries the system and can be controlled to guide it through intermediate waypoints toward the desired destination. The resulting framework provides a GPS-free navigation mechanism with potential applications in both engineering and biology. In engineering, it can be used to establish a geomagnetic navigation infrastructure through which prescribed routes can be defined and followed, while in biology, it can be used to analyse the migration routes of animals known to rely on magnetoreception.

record.title: Wilson loops of Chern-Simons-matter Theories with one parameter and Picard-Fuchs equations
record.abstract: Extending our previous work, we investigate Wilson loops of flavored Chern-Simons theory and ABJ theory by the use of Picard-Fuchs equations. The singularity structure of the equations is analyzed in detail, and local solutions around the singularities are determined. Each theory has one parameter, and the parameter dependence of the Wilson loops is also determined. In flavored Chern-Simons theory, we find an interesting phase transition. For $n$-times-wound Wilson loops, we determine their $n$-dependence by using a recursion relation obtained in our previous work.

record.title: Algebraic flat bands and even central-band Chern numbers in a seven-orbital hopping model
record.abstract: Turning a flat-band parent into an isolated Chern band requires supervise of destructive interference, hopping phases, and the cell translations of the bonds. We study this connection in a seven-orbital 2 times 2 supercell honeycomb-vacancy lattice, combining analytic reductions with Bloch spectra, lattice Chern invariants, and quantum geometry. The parent lattice has three exact flat branches, a smooth periodic zero mode, and a compact localized state. A uniform gap bound shows that faint intracell-loop hopping preserves two topologically trivial insulating gaps. The intracell hopping graph also admits a staggered chiral coloring: reversing site amplitudes according to this coloring links opposite energies at momenta separated by half a reciprocal period. This constraint restricts the isolated central band to even Chern numbers and forbids a zero-energy insulating filling at every loop phase. Purely imaginary loop hopping admits a real gauge, whereas other phases allow paired band contacts connecting central bands with C3=2 and C3=4. On a specified strong-loop cut, third-order masses open the direct gaps; these gaps shrink faster than the bandwidth as the coupling grows. Changing the bond connectivity to an oriented honeycomb next-nearest-neighbor extension generates a narrower Chern band with nonuniform quantum geometry. These results distinguish individual-band topology from occupied-group topology and reveal how bond connectivity and cell translations determine which topological bands can emerge from an exactly flat parent.

record.title: Readout and Operating-Point Sensitivity in Event-Stream Candidate Selection
record.abstract: Event-triggered recording needs a useful combination of target capture and false triggers, yet representation comparisons can change with readout and threshold calibration. We evaluate real event accumulations from 520 DailyDVS-200 clips and 47 participants using participant-disjoint training, validation, and testing. The original study varies frozen encoder scale, accumulation duration, and temporal view count; a post-review extension adds two supervised-pretrained convolutional encoders, a 61,586-parameter trained CNN with three seeds, ten repeated participant partitions, and calibration sensitivity. At 50 ms/eight views under the primary handshake-or-fall policy, DINO-S CLS captures 101/132 targets with 40/388 false triggers, versus 78/132 and 35/388 for patch mean. DINO-B CLS has lower selected-threshold capture but higher fold-wise low-FPR partial AUC (0.746 versus 0.732). MobileNetV3-Small captures 97/132 with 53/388 false triggers, demonstrating why lightweight baselines and actual operating points matter. Across ten dependent repartitions, mean normalized partial AUC is 0.738 for DINO-B CLS and 0.674 for MobileNet. The original LeJEPA S-to-B capture difference is 8.3 points, but its multiplicity-adjusted interval includes zero. Duration and view-count effects remain policy dependent. We find no established JEPA-specific advantage. The evidence concerns offline action-defined candidate selection on previously used development data; it does not establish personal recording value, continuous false alarms per hour, or eyewear energy.

record.title: Kinetic Sectors and Nonequilibrium Dynamics in the $δ$-Ising Model
record.abstract: We introduce and analyze the $δ$-Ising model, a kinetic Ising ferromagnet in which single-spin flips are accepted when their energy change does not exceed a tunable threshold. Varying the field and threshold opens or closes local flip channels, dividing parameter space into kinetic sectors, each governed by a fixed Markov transition operator. We prove that the dynamics retains global spin-inversion symmetry exactly when up and down spins have equal numbers of open channels. In one such sector on a periodic chain of length $L$, unbiased random initial states therefore reach the field-aligned and antifield states with probability $1/2$ each. Closing a single channel leaves both states absorbing but makes the probability of ordering against the field decay as $(2/π)^L$. Parameter sweeps correspond to ordered products of sector operators, which separate reaching a state from holding it, so hysteresis appears when a state is reached and released at different sector boundaries. We also show how increasing the system size can induce a Mpemba-like reversal, allowing a state with more misaligned spins to reach the final ordered state sooner on average. On a periodic chain, this reversal arises because the mean absorption time grows logarithmically with system size for many short domains but linearly for a single macroscopic domain, and it disappears when the bulk flip channel is opened. These findings show how a simple, intuitive rule for Ising dynamics links local kinetic constraints to field response, memory, and relaxation within a unified framework.

record.title: Personality Latents: Conditioning Frozen Language Models on Individuals from Their Own Writing
record.abstract: Controlling the personality of a language model usually relies on written profiles or named trait categories, so it can only express what an author writes down or what a taxonomy names. We instead propose Personality Latents (PL), which learn a latent for each person from their own writing, with no personality labels and no authored profile, and inject it into a frozen language model as a soft prefix. Following generative latent optimization, each training person receives a free latent that is optimized through the frozen model itself, while an encoder learns to predict these latents so that a new person needs only one forward pass, with optional refinement at test time. We evaluate on held-out people by having the conditioned model answer neutral and interview questions and reading personality from its answers with scorers trained on real human writing. On the MBTI axes PL reaches an AUC of , ahead of persona embedding and prompt-based baselines under identical settings, and the ranking holds when the answers are scored in three different embedding spaces. A latent learned with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct also transfers personality to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct through a new adapter alone.

record.title: A Unified Protocol for Arbitrary Z Rotations of a Class of Bosonic cQED Qubits
record.abstract: Bosonic-qubit encodings provide diverse approaches to storing and processing quantum information, with logical operations often implemented through encoding-specific physical strategies. Here, we identify a class of bosonic Fock-based qubits in circuit QED for which distinct implementations of arbitrary Z rotations share a common structure. We formulate this structure as a six-step protocol that provides a unified procedure for implementing arbitrary Z rotations across this class of bosonic cQED qubits. The applicability of the protocol is determined by a specific condition on the encoding, providing a criterion for identifying bosonic Fock-based cQED qubits that admit the common implementation.

record.title: Variable-Length Feedback Coding With Universal Decoding and Bandit Channel Selection
record.abstract: We study variable-length feedback (VLF) coding over $K$ additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels whose noise variances are unknown to both terminals but lie in a known interval. The receiver selects one channel at each time, conveys the selection over noiseless feedback, and must learn the channel qualities while decoding, to avoid overusing suboptimal channels. This setting, which we call the VLF-Bandit problem, combines VLF coding, universal decoding, and bandit channel selection. We develop two joint coding and channel-selection schemes. The VLSF-Bandit scheme is a single-phase variable-length stop-feedback (VLSF) scheme based on a Gaussian random codebook, a score formed from a ratio of likelihood mixtures, and the asymptotically optimal $\text{kl-UCB}^{++}$ bandit algorithm applied to the received power. The VLF-Bandit scheme sends the message in packets by Schalkwijk--Kailath transmission, uses its normalized outputs as noise samples to learn the variances, and lets its exploration packets carry message bits. We prove second-order achievability bounds for both schemes, which are first-order optimal. In the logarithm of the achievable codebook size, the magnitude of the $\log N$ coefficient, with $N$ the average decoding time, is a baseline of one plus a channel-exploration term for VLSF-Bandit. For VLF-Bandit, this magnitude is smaller, with a universal-decoding term replacing the baseline and a smaller channel-exploration term. The VLF-Bandit bound improves on the universal VLF bound of Yavas and Tan (2025) for $K=1$ and on the bound of an explore-then-commit strategy whenever $K\geq2$.

record.title: The dynamics of MM: Einstein's weak field, Friedmann's cosmology, and a boundary set by the Galaxy, with a registered test on Gaia DR4 wide binaries
record.publication: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
record.abstract: This record. The dynamics of the framework: Einstein's weak field, Friedmann's cosmology and a boundary set by the Galaxy, with a registered test on Gaia DR4 wide binaries. Reading path: Galaxies and the cosmic scale a₀ = cH₀/6, 5 of 6 · before: Cassini and the wide-binary signal · next: Galaxy clusters and a turned spacetime · all themes. Common introduction to all the records of this series. The content of this record follows below. Mathematical Materiality (MM) in brief. Why are the laws of physics the same everywhere and at every instant, even though nothing forces matter to obey them? MM proposes an answer: the laws are not rules imposed on matter from the outside; rather, matter itself is made of mathematical relations. And mathematics cannot change: a relation binds two distinct terms everywhere and always. In logic, nothing exists on its own: to exist means to be in relation to another logical entity, and outside this web of relations nothing can exist, not even other universes. This reading already meets experimental measurements at two points. First, the ratio of dark to ordinary matter is read as 3√3 = 5.196; when left free in the fits, Planck and DESI DR2 data give 5.21–5.22 (as registered in record 2.44, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23329080). Second, the acceleration scale of galaxies is read as a₀ = cH₀/6, the same scale that appears in Verlinde's emergent gravity: the computed value is 1.09–1.18 × 10⁻¹⁰ m/s² against the measured value of 1.20 (record 2.46.1, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23506655). Both readings were formulated with the measurements already known; the tests to check them against future data are registered in the same records. In the first logical nexus between space and time — which became homogeneous with Einstein — there is a non-local phase, made only of a pure logical distinction: space is not time. Between the two there is no relation of quantitative calculation, only the logical entity they have in common, which is needed to make them exist with respect to each other. This level is not distant: it is present in every phase of reality, in every place and at every instant. It shows in entanglement, where two distant systems remain correlated more strongly than any explanation based on separate properties and free of faster-than-light influences allows, without anything physically travelling between them. In this non-local phase the two distinct terms, space and time, share only one logical element, which we shall call their greatest common divisor (GCD), just as the numbers 3 and 5 have only 1 in common. The local world arises when a relation is counted through this GCD: its multiples and its fractions form a matrix. Seen by an observer inside the system like us, the multiples appear as time and the fractions as space. When that same multiple is directly contained in the matrix of the point of observation, it turns into mass — that is, into concrete matter as we usually understand it. There is therefore a close link between time and mass, in full agreement with Einstein's relativity, which ties mass to spacetime. The observed objects, while being logically autonomous entities in their local relations, enter into relation with the observer through a logical diffraction — that is, a decomposition into fractions — of the observer's matrix. This reading also gives a reason for the limit of the speed of light, which in Einstein's relativity is instead taken as a starting principle. The speed of light is the fixed exchange rate between the multiples and the fractions of the same GCD, meaning how much space a single step of time is worth: exceeding it would mean, for some observer, covering space without counting time, and thus leaving the local world. Logic always starts from a logical relative, and this exchange rate has nothing absolute in itself either: it is a necessary relative which, inside the system, becomes an absolute hypothesis, the same for everyone and impossible to exceed. Outside the system, by contrast, it has no justification at all, because outside there is only non-existence: justifying something requires another term to relate it to, and out there there is none. Asking for a reason from outside is like asking what lies north of the North Pole. The same theoretical framework that reads space, time, mass and the observed objects also admits quantum mechanics. The non-local phase and the mirror-like logical reciprocity between the two ends of the nexus give a reason for the probabilistic behaviour of matter. When the observed object is large enough, its mass fixes it in the matrix of the point of observation: for this reason we see it in one precise place and at one precise instant. When instead the object falls below a certain mass threshold, the principal GCD (that of the point of observation) and the GCD of the diffraction that generates the object are forced to become equal, reflecting each other as in a mirror. At that point the object no longer occupies a single point of the spacetime generated by the observer, but spreads over several possible positions, and we observe it as probability. It is like having to describe the number 10 using only the number 1: the only way is to distribute the 1 over ten positions, one for each unit of the 10. Today we know that even objects made of thousands of atoms behave in this way, and no experiment has yet found the boundary. The idea that the passage from quantum to classical behaviour depends on mass is close to that of Penrose and Diósi; in MM the threshold is the point where the two GCDs, the principal one and that of the local diffraction, become equal. For all these reasons the universe behaves like a simulation without really being one. It follows exact rules, made of counts, everywhere and at every instant, but no machine runs them and no programmer wrote them: a structure of mathematical relations does not need to be computed in order to exist. Tegmark (2008) had already noted that such a simulation need not be run, while Vazza (2025) estimated that running it physically on a machine would require resources that the very laws of the universe do not allow. This record develops one aspect of the theoretical framework. The work is shared openly so that it can be judged by as many readers as possible: anyone who knows someone interested can pass on this single link, valid for the whole framework (with an overview in English and Italian): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23535916. The entry page, with the complete list of all records, is https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22667516. To cite the framework: Lanciano, U. (2026). Objections and errors found are welcome at riverantares@gmail.com, since Zenodo has no space for comments. This record gives the dynamics of Mathematical Materiality (MM). In the weak field it is linearised Einstein gravity, and the homogeneous model is Friedmann's. record.title: The Wess-Zumino Action of the Conformal Anomaly
record.abstract: The complete Wess-Zumino (WZ) action and stress-energy tensor (SET) of the conformal anomaly in both two and four dimensions is given. This local effective action is expressed in terms of a single scalar Nambu-Goldstone `conformalon' field $\varphi$, parametrizing the local abelian Weyl group of conformal transformations that act transitively on the spacetime metric. Satisfying WZ consistency, and equipped with a variational principle for $\varphi$ that determines the conformal transformation $g_{μν}\!\to\!g_{μν}e^{-\varphi}$ to an associated spacetime with no anomaly, the WZ action resolves the conformal gauge fixing ambiguity of earlier methods of `integrating the anomaly.' In $D\!=\!2$ the WZ action is the local form of the Polyakov action, whose massless $\varphi$ propagator describes a correlated two-particle scalar intermediate state in the SET polarization function $\langle TT\rangle$. The imaginary part of this polarization obeys a UV finite sum rule, becoming a Dirac $δ$-function at zero energy for conformal quantum fields, demonstrating the infrared origin of the anomaly, while the real part becomes the light cone propagator of $\varphi$. Although the $\Box R$ term in $D\!=\!4$ corresponds to a cohomologically trivial cocycle, it also arises from the IR limit of massless quantum fields, independently of UV physics, and contributes to the WZ action for low energy gravity. Analogous to the WZ action for pseudo-Goldstone mesons in low energy QCD from the axial anomaly, the WZ action for the conformal anomaly provides a Nambu-Goldstone scalar field for macroscopic gravity, in addition to the metric of classical general relativity.

record.title: Calibrated sequential mergers of three Jordan blocks under the Aluthge transform
record.publication: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
record.abstract: Three fixed Jordan blocks are joined by two positive links that vanish as positive powers of a small parameter. A candidate joint limit is given for ordinary half Aluthge iteration when the two initial crossover exponents are strictly ordered. The first merger changes the background seen by the remaining link and accelerates the second merger. For blocks of sizes p, q and r, when the last two merge first, links aε^α and bε^β give late exponent 4[α+βr/(q+r)]/(p+q+r) and matrix entrance amplitude a b^(r/(q+r)) [2^(p+q+r−2)(p−1)!(q+r−1)!]^(−1/2). Both discrete profile limits are uniform on compact positive crossover windows in a specified moving triangular gauge. The proposed proof combines a graded early passage, a uniform estimate through the interval between mergers and an exact weighted-product identity, which calibrates the late entrance without a normalized matrix-variation assumption through the first merger. Block sizes, positive coefficients, powers and the strict ordering gap are fixed. The balanced simultaneous case, shrinking separation gaps, complex phases and quantitative error rates are outside the result. The theorem retains candidate status; the established-status verification threshold has not been met.

record.title: Network analysis of rare single-nucleotide polymorphisms suggests a central role for type 17 immune responses in trauma-induced, genotypically associated hypo-inflammation and critical illness
record.abstract: ABSTRACT Critical illness stemming from severe traumatic injury is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, involves the dysfunction of multiple organ systems, and is driven at least in part by dysregulated inflammation that involves type 17 immunity. We and others have demonstrated a genetic predisposition to adverse critical illness outcomes associated with single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in novel loci distinct from those which impact type 17 immune responses yet acting in concert with those responses. We have recently developed SNPScanner , an algorithm that enables rapid scanning through a large SNP dataset and associated inflammation biomarkers and clinical data, and in the present study leveraged this algorithm in concert with existing bioinformatics tools to define networks of interaction among rare SNPs (defined operationally as being present in 5-10% of patients due to the study cohort size) assessed in critically ill trauma patients. RAR-related orphan receptor A (RORA), a transcription factor central to the differentiation of Th17 cells, was inferred as a hub gene via its SNP rs4774381; stratification of trauma patients based on homozygous genotype at this SNP pointed to distinct organ dysfunction trajectories associated with network-defined hypo-inflammation. Further, the SNP rs11919443 in the non-hub TM4SF19 gene distinguished genotype-associated systemic IL-17A trajectories, and associated hypo-inflammation with adverse outcomes. In contrast, no Th17-related hub genes were identified in a control group of SNPs associated algorithmically with adverse clinical outcomes but with genotypically indistinct systemic inflammatory responses; the main inferred hub gene in this control group was solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 1 ( SLC2A1 )/glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1). Secondary analysis showed several statistically significant differences in circulating inflammatory mediators not including IL-17A, and also associated network-based hypo-inflammation with adverse outcomes in this control group. This study thus extends our prior work aimed at defining genetic predisposition to dysregulated inflammation and pathophysiology in the context of critical illness, and points to a crucial role for type 17 immune responses.

record.title: On surfaces, that fill the space
record.abstract: The article is devoted to the construction of dimension-raising maps of cubes with the highest possible Holder exponent. In particular, a square-to-cube mapping with a Holder exponent of $2/3$ is constructed, which is a solution to the V.I.Arnold problem.

record.title: Tribocharging of Granular Materials Dictated by Geometric and Thermoelectric Effects
record.abstract: Tribocharging of granular materials is a widespread phenomenon ranging from volcanic eruptions and dust storms to pharmaceutical processing, yet its underlying mechanism remains elusive. Recent thermoelectric models have provided a quantitative framework for triboelectric charge transfer, but they have difficulty accounting for charging between identical materials. In this Letter, we propose a theory of granular tribocharging based on the interplay between particle geometry and thermoelectric response. Collision-induced frictional heating produces a size-dependent temperature asymmetry between particles, generating a thermoelectric voltage that drives charge transfer. The sign of the Seebeck coefficient determines the charging polarity, while particle size and thermal properties set its magnitude. Our multi-collision theory explains the experimentally observed size- and material-dependent reversal of charging polarity, as in quartz and nylon.

record.title: Extracting the QCD speed of sound in the presence of quantum fluctuations
record.abstract: The equation of state of strongly interacting matter plays a %is one of the central quantities characterizing central role in characterizing quark--gluon plasma created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. It has recently been recognized that the QCD speed of sound is responsible for the linear correlations between the mean transverse momentum and charged-particle multiplicity in ultra-central collisions. In realistic collisions, however, this thermodynamic correlation is inevitably biased by quantum-initiated event-by-event fluctuations. In this work, we present a novel statistical framework to correct this bias by leveraging the Gaussianity condition of the quantum fluctuations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this approach can also serve as a probe of thermalization. Validated by the event-by-event hydrodynamic simulations, the extracted speed of sound in our framework is successfully consistent with the predictions from lattice QCD, from large to small collision systems.

record.title: Information Looking for Its Owner in DNA Repair
record.publication: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
record.abstract: Ultraviolet light writes a mark into DNA: two neighbouring pyrimidines fuse into a cyclobutane pyrimidine dimer (CPD). The mark is information without an owner. Somewhere among billions of intact base pairs, a set of proteins has to find it, confirm it, cut it out and rewrite the gap. This application note borrows a way of asking questions, not a result, from a protocol written for a different system, the freezing of supercooled water (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23724281), and applies it to nucleotide excision repair. Three things transfer: a separation of five roles (source, carrier, processor, state builder, meaning-giver); the idea that what matters is the irreversible act, not the state it leaves behind; and a control that spends the same energy with the same machinery but produces no record. In repair, that control is the full excision system working on undamaged DNA. One thing does not transfer: the clock effect that Time-Gel Theory attaches to irreversible events is about 10^-11 s per cell, far below any clock that could sit inside a cell. The note proposes a biochemical experiment that measures what it costs, in ATP, for information to find its correct owner, and whether paying less produces more wrong owners. Conventional kinetic proofreading, proposed for this step by Reardon and Sancar (2003), predicts the same outcomes; the note claims no discrimination. It then takes a first look at a public CPD Damage-seq time course in human fibroblasts (Hu et al., PNAS 2017). Thirty-six hours after UV, about 17% of the genome sits in 100 kb bins whose damage has not gone down at all; these bins form blocks with a mean length of about 560 kb and are concentrated on chromosomes 21, X, 13 and 18. This note does not test Time-Gel Theory. Every claim is labelled (MEASURED, OBSERVED, MODEL, HYPOTHESIS, DECISION, OPEN, INTERPRETATION, ANALOGY).

record.title: Lead-pattern potentials and exact values of merging networks
record.publication: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
record.abstract: Let M(m,n) be the least number of comparators in a network that merges sorted lists of lengths m and n. We prove M(5,7) = 18, M(6,8) = 22, M(6,9) = 25, M(7,9) = 27 and M(5,15) = 35, five values listed as open in 2009, together with M(5,10) = 25, M(5,11) = 27, M(5,12) = 29 and M(6,10) = 27, for which we know of no published determination. In all nine cases Batcher's odd-even merge is optimal. Each lead of a network computes a monotone Boolean function of its input, and a comparator replaces two such functions by their disjunction and conjunction, so a potential on these functions that grows by at most one at each comparator bounds the size of the network from below. The best such bound is the optimum of a linear program. For merging networks its solutions round to exact rational certificates, which two separately written programs check, and the nine values are also proved in Lean 4, partly by compiled code. Closed-form potentials give new proofs of the formulas for M(2,n) and M(3,n), of the odd cases of M(4,n), and of Iwata's linear coefficient. The certificates, the checkers and the logs of all computations are archived as doi:10.5281/zenodo.23719457, and the Lean proofs as doi:10.5281/zenodo.23719459.
